name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
hint: The harbour must stay clear below the road. Spring an arch from the low anchors, rise high above the deck and hang the road from it.

history.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
history.engineer: John Bradfield; designed and built by Dorman Long & Co (Ralph Freeman)
history.span: Arch span 503 m · top 134 m above the water
facts: The two half-arches were built out from each shore, held back by cables anchored in tunnels, until they met on 19 August 1930.
About six million rivets, all driven by hand, hold together 52,800 tonnes of steel.
The four granite-faced pylons carry nothing - they were added for looks and to reassure the public.
history.why: Nicknamed "The Coathanger", it carries eight road lanes, two railway tracks, a footway and a cycleway, and was the world's widest long-span bridge until 2012.
